rules: Decompose before filing (itd-84, adopted 2026-08-15 at the MVP rung): before filing an intent, run the hand-run four-piece table documented in the /abcd:intent surface page — each part routed to its record home (capability -> intent; trust rule -> ADR + brief invariant; stance -> principle; plumbing -> brief), verdict FILE-AS-IS / SPLIT / HOLD, and a human confirms the routing.

Cross-record links are typed — supersedes / reverses / duplicates / refines — never a vague 'related'. A reversal flag is advisory-only: flagged for the human to confirm, never auto-classified, never auto-filed.

Not yet automated (loud-staging): the deterministic pre-pass and the capture-time validator are future rungs; until they ship the documented protocol is the gate. Grade every hand-run into the dated decomposition-calibration research note — the corpus that gates the automated rung.

Read the where-to-look playbook before hunting: .abcd/development/research/notes/2026-07-17-bug-hunting-principles.md — the spine, the value-ordered checklist (smell · failing question · CWE anchor), and the known gaps.

Spine: most defects are a wrong implicit assumption at a trust boundary that fails SILENTLY (ASCII-only, SHA-1-only, case-sensitive, one control range, first-occurrence-wins, clean env, parseable config). A fix is not done until every sibling site is swept — grep the pattern, not the instance.

Highest-leverage move: for each hardened primitive (gitutil.IsolatedEnv, fsutil.ReadGuarded, fsutil.WriteFileAtomic, refIsSafe, the (?i) identity matchers, lifeboat sanitize), grep for the unhardened sibling (raw os.Environ/os.ReadFile/os.WriteFile, a positional git arg, a case-sensitive matcher, a raw terminal print) and prove each is hardened or explicitly out of scope under the trusted-worktree model.
Markdown is the single source of truth; HTML is a generated, disposable artefact.
Docs are present tense only — what IS, never what was superseded or planned.
One Diataxis type per page (tutorial / how-to / reference / explanation).
User-facing prose in British English; code-side identifiers, comments, strings in US English.

Writing style: Follow the canonical guide at docs/reference/writing-style.md — em dashes allowed in prose but never in list items (use a colon), a capital letter after a colon, lower case after a semicolon. The guide labels each rule machine-enforced or review (the list-item em-dash rule is enforced as a docs-lint banned token; adr-54 rules the colon and semicolon casing checks review by nature); point at the guide rather than copying it.
Intents are press-release-first; acceptance criteria are BDD (Given/When/Then).

Personas come from .abcd/development/personas.json: pick by role, never by name, and refer to every persona as they/them. The persona_registry record-lint rule enforces the registry (itd-79). (The bundled default names Alice/Bob/Carol for a registry-less adopter; this repo ships the registry, so the roster is the full fourteen.)
Lifecycle is drafts/ -> planned/ -> shipped/; a planned intent's adoption is a maintainer decision.
